text: Two things were in dispute. First, the card's own embedded Description ("`BUILTIN` gains `'chores': ('PostToolUse',)`" and a `{name: callable}` `cmd_hook` dispatch mapping) contradicts the approved, trunk-current replan `docs/plans/replans/f-0035-03bc1192bd10.md` (Task T-0192, lines 255-317), which instead gives `cmd_hook` a third explicit `'chores'` branch and never touches `BUILTIN`/`ACCOUNT_HOOKS`. Checked against the checkout: `asf/hooks.py:65,70` defines `BUILTIN = {'approvals': ('PreToolUse',), 'unpushed': ('Stop',)}` and `ACCOUNT_HOOKS = tuple((event, name) for name, events in BUILTIN.items() ...)`, written into every worker account's settings unconditionally by the `for account in accounts: _write_merged(...)` loop at `:696-697`; folding `'chores'` into `BUILTIN` as the stale Description says would put the recorder into every worker account's settings, which breaks this very card's own acceptance ("no worker account gets the entry") and §1.4 of the spec. The stale Description is OVERRULED; the replan's third-branch dispatch design holds and needs no further planning round. Second, the card's `after:` still names a dead predecessor (`T-0190` / "Task 2" in the stale Description); the replan already found that card gone from F-0035's open Tasks and replaced it with `T-0189` (lines 260-266), the Task that owns `asf/chores.py` - confirmed absent from this checkout (no `asf/chores.py`, `asf/tick/step_watch.py`, or `rules/controller-chores.sh` anywhere in the tree), the exact module T-0192's own dispatch branch imports (`from asf import chores; chores.record(...)`). That dependency is UPHELD: a dangling `after:` is the likely reason the dependency gate kept releasing this card into CODE before its real predecessor existed, producing the PLAN<->CODE churn. `writes:` is unchanged - `asf/hooks.py tests/test_install.py` already matches the replan's own `writes:` line exactly, and the test scaffolding it needs (`tests/test_hooks.py`; `HooksApprovalTests`/`HooksTest` in `tests/test_install.py:1377,1438`) is already on the trunk - so once T-0189 lands this Task is immediately codeable straight from the replan, with no new plan or review needed.

Disputed: the spec-amend session that declared F-0121's six Stories (commit f2dd68a, S-68354..S-68359, from its own claimed block) left the plan's five Tasks citing the ids the spec carried before that renumbering (S-32700..S-32705, docs/plans/f-0121.md PD5 and PD13, verified against the checkout) — ids that were never cards and are now declared nowhere, so asf.record.plan_tasks.stories_of would drop them from every minted Task and the plan has no "## Stories" section for phantom_stories to catch it, so minting would silently lose the Story-to-Task links (exactly the NEEDS OPERATOR the last report raised: "the replan re-cites S-68354..S-68359 or the plan's stories: lines are corrected in place"). Upheld, corrected in place rather than by replan: PD13's second premise — that asf.record.plan_tasks.STORY_ID_RE only matches four-digit ids — is itself stale, verified against asf/record/plan_tasks.py:35 and asf/record/core.py:45 in this checkout: fix(F-0285) #1046 already widened it to ID_DIGITS (four or more digits) after docs/plans/f-0113.md's PD15 raised the same defect, so a renumbered id mints correctly once the spec's declared Stories are minted ahead of the Tasks (asf/record/plan_tasks.py:190-219). I renumbered the five stories: lines (Tasks 1-5) one to one onto S-68354..S-68359 in PD5's own order, and rewrote PD5 and PD13 to say so, on commit 465395e. This closes the NO STORIES -> SPEC-AMEND cycle: the next tick's plan-tasks pass mints the six Stories from the spec's declared headings and then the five Tasks, each now citing a Story id that is already a card, so has_stories is satisfied and the loop does not reopen. Overruled: none. Carried forward, not litigated here: the second NEEDS OPERATOR in the last report (spec-amend-f-0121, commit f2dd68a) — asf.record.idcheck.declared_stories reads a declared Story through _prose, which blanks every backtick span, mangling any title or acceptance line that cites a backticked identifier (reproducible today against docs/specs/f-0056.md's S-67204) — is a defect in idcheck shared by every spec that declares Stories, not specific to F-0121's stalemate, and this session has no backlog access to mint the Bug it needs.
NEEDS OPERATOR: asf.record.idcheck.declared_stories (asf/record/idcheck.py:99-109) reads a declared Story's title and acceptance lines through _prose, which replaces every code span with a single space before the regex runs, so a backticked identifier anywhere in a `### S-…` heading or its checkbox lines is silently blanked out of what the record would mint. docs/specs/f-0056.md is already on the trunk working around it by writing its six declared Stories with no backticks at all; F-0121's spec does the same. Ruling: the sketch ids are dead — the record never held S-32650..S-32653 and an ingest mapping has nothing to resolve them against — so the plan's four `stories:` lines and the test docstring are corrected directly to S-68654..S-68657 on this branch; a replan is not needed for a one-to-one id correction and none recurs. The root cause closes with docs/specs/f-0111.stories.sh, the mint script the spec-amend session should have left (as F-0069 and F-0092 did for the identical gap), built from that session's own claimed block, ready for a factory-host session to run. SPEC-AMEND is not tried a fourth time: there is nothing left in the spec to amend, only a mint to run.

Disputed: the "NO STORIES -> SPEC-AMEND" hold, stuck for three rounds. Each prior round read the spec's P17 (and the plan's PD16), which measured plan_tasks.STORY_ID_RE as the literal `\bS-\d{4}\b` and concluded a five-digit Story id could never match it, so every round left the `## Stories` section as a plain bullet list quoting a long-expired session's placeholder ids (S-39150..S-39155) instead of declaring real ones. Checked against the checkout at HEAD d439d8d9: `asf/record/core.py:45` defines `ID_DIGITS = r'\d{4,}'` (four *or more* digits), so `plan_tasks.STORY_ID_RE` already matches a five-digit id and measurably always did in this checkout (`STORY_ID_RE.findall('S-39150, S-39151')` -> `['S-39150', 'S-39151']`) — the four-digit reading was stale, not a defect, and was never the real blocker. The actual, still-live gap: neither the spec nor the plan ever wrote a `### S-id: <title>` heading with checkbox acceptance lines underneath — the one shape `asf.record.idcheck.declared_stories` reads and `asf.record.plan_tasks._mint` mints from unconditionally once a session's claim covers the id (`asf/record/plan_tasks.py:188-210`; no `## Stories`-citation check gates minting — that check only catches a bare citation with no heading behind it). What now holds: upheld — the spec's `## Stories` section now declares all six Stories as `### S-id: <title>` headings with checkbox acceptance lines, under this adjudicating session's own claimed block `S:69404-69453` (S-69404..S-69409, replacing the stale quoted ids); the spec's frontmatter and the plan's six per-Task `stories:` lines are updated to match; P17 and PD16 are corrected to the current measurement. Verified directly against `idcheck.declared_stories`/`cited_stories`/`phantom_stories`: all six declare, cite and mint clean, with zero phantoms. What changes: once this branch lands on `main`, `plan_tasks._mint` will mint the six Story cards the next time the tick ingests the plan, ending the stalemate without any further spec-amend round — the loop restarts only if a later round removes these headings.

Disputed: whether a fourth SPEC-AMEND round could ever satisfy NO STORIES for F-0129 after three rounds of the identical cycle. Overruled — it cannot. docs/specs/f-0129.md already declares its six Stories exactly as the system's own cloud-session fallback asks for (`### S-68754:`..`### S-68759:` headings with checkbox acceptance lines, ids from a claimed block — asf/briefs/build.py:707-712, the STORIES_FIRST brief). The gate that keeps firing, `asf.feeder.rows.has_stories` (asf/feeder/rows.py:421-425), reads only the record's own Story children, never a spec's prose; a declared heading becomes a card only when a Task-bearing plan for this Feature lands (asf/record/plan_tasks.py:190-215 mints the fixed ids straight off the `## Stories` heading). F-0129 is already at stage plan-approved with Task children from its original, long-landed plan, so that ingest pass has already run once for this Feature and is a permanent no-op on it per the module's own docstring ("A Feature that already has a Task child is left alone... a re-run is a no-op"); nothing re-triggers it short of a replan, and a replan starts only once the Feature's card carries an operator's `reshape:` answer (asf/record/replan.py:106-112; asf/groom/groom.py:44-45,883-909) — a write no session in this pipeline, cloud or otherwise, can make without record access. So each of the three prior spec-amend sessions did the one thing available to a cloud session and NO STORIES was always going to fire again regardless of what any of them wrote; a fourth would be no different. What changes: committed docs/specs/f-0129.stories.sh on this branch — six `asf new story --parent F-0129 …` calls (ids S-69554..S-69559, this session's claimed block), positional to the spec's six declared Stories, for a session with real record access to run once — the same remedy already used for F-0069 and F-0092 (docs/specs/f-0069.stories.sh, docs/specs/f-0092.stories.sh). Once run, `has_stories` is satisfied immediately and the NO STORIES cycle clears with no replan needed. Whether F-0129's existing Tasks (cut from its original plan, which predates every one of these spec-amend rounds) still match the current spec's design is a separate question this adjudication has not examined — no record access reaches the actual Task cards from here — and is not decided by this ruling; an overruled NO STORIES finding does not come back in a later round, but a plan/Task mismatch, if real, would surface as its own issue.
